㊣ ("14 ptoblems is plenty") Agreed, coverage isn't the limit for one night. Both loops are active.

㊟ (what I'll watch instead) The thing to watch is how quickly rows end in STOP. Three rows so far ended with the author stopping and the reviewer passing that stop: t96A07 closure, t99J04 reroute, and the topo2 polygon-quotient row. Some took only a minute or two. If the loops keep stopping like that, they'll use up those 14 problems by morning without closing many. If the watch wakes me overnight, I'll read the stop reasons before I refill anything.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-14
previous_reply_acts.text:
(why the progress will be modest)
- **Coverage.** The two ledgers have live rows for only about 14 problems (t98J02, t99J04, t99J05, t94J09, t96A07, t95A04, t02A02, t00J07, t94A08, …). The others get rows only when a strategy checkpoint elects new routes.
- **topo1 will need a refill.** After its 3 remaining rows, topo1 reaches its refill checkpoint. The previous one answered "terminal": every other route was held by the stop-after-two rule. If that happens again, the loop pauses, which happened on 09-29 too and needed a manual refill.
- **topo2 is refilling itself.** Its strategy step wrote four new rows today (`routes-2026-10-10-*`).
- **Quota is fine.** The Codex weekly window is at 12%.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-14
previous_reply_acts.text: (what I set up) `~/topo-watch/overnight-watch.sh` is running under bg.py (`bg-1791603763559-308`). Every 10 minutes it checks both units. If either is inactive, or its log has been silent for 75 minutes, it bells me in work mode to act as owner: refill a paused ledger, or repair and relaunch a stopped loop. It sends at most one bell per loop every 90 minutes. I set its end time to "tomorrow 09:00" UTC, which works out to 10-11 09:00, a day later than I meant. It's harmless and covers your whole day; `bg.py kill` stops it.

previous_reply_acts.text: (first results since restart) Two reviews have come back. To compare in the morning, run `~/topo-watch/check.py`; it prints closures and reopenings since the last check.
